title: RAW two directional influences retain the same iron patient under an explicit adamant context
summary: RAW UNREVIEWED. Complete owned Steele id00097 keeps iron as the shared patient of magnet drawing and adamant drawing away, after adamant is set by it. The concession about the magnet must be distinguished from the prevented approach. The whole paragraph also names the stone of reconciliation/love and gives a qualified, disjunctive woman–husband reconciliation claim; these cannot be discarded or collapsed into one physical law.

source.work: Robert Steele, Mediaeval Lore from Bartholomew Anglicus, Project Gutenberg 6493, chapter I, complete paragraph id00097
source.edition_status: Already owned edited English anthology. Its introductory id00038 dates the quoted Trevisa translation to1397; the anthology attributes the underlying work to the thirteenth century. These are edition statements, not a newly collated medieval witness or an original-language notation claim.
source.boundary: Every word of id00097, If an adamant be set by iron through have grace of her husband. The complete parent chapter was already owned; this task directly reread this full paragraph and selected neighboring units, not all64 blocks.

design.hypothesis: A whole-content account may preserve a shared patient while contrasting one named influence directed toward a second object with a competing influence directed away from that object. The written conditional changes the context, and the concessive clause preserves a magnet-drawing claim rather than simply erasing that claim. This is an exploratory source-content mechanism, not an assigned Voynich meaning.
explicit_argument_ownership: Iron in the placement condition, the prevented approach, it after draweth, and iron/it in the explanatory concession refer to the same hypothetical patient. Splitting them into convenient different iron portions changes the local anaphoric content.

Adamant is the subject of suffereth not and the first draweth; the later named adamant confirms the competing actor. Magnet is the named goal of come/drawing-to and the reference object of drawing-away. The reflexive itself in the magnet clause refers to the magnet, not the iron or adamant.
Placement by iron is explicit. No initial contact of iron with magnet, completed arrival, quantified displacement, speed, force, duration or measured motion is supplied.

The later It/this stone retains the named stone kind. The hypothetical woman and her husband are locally co-referent through away/trespass/reconciliation/grace. The mineral and marriage cases do not establish one particular physical stone used twice.
whole_content_duties: Conditional setting: an adamant set by iron. Preserve by as the contextual spatial relation; do not replace it with contact or mixing.
Prevention: the iron is not suffered to come to the magnet. The source attributes prevention to adamant; it does not say the magnet ceases to have its described power.
Competing direction: the adamant draws the iron by a manner of violence from the magnet. Preserve the qualified manner phrase without inventing a numerical force.

Explanatory concession: though the magnet draws iron to itself, adamant draws it away from magnet. Retain the magnet claim, patient sharing and opposite direction. The historical assertion is not a validated physical law.
Naming: it is called a precious stone of reconciliation and love. Reported naming is distinct from the following claimed effect.

Human conditional: if a woman is away from her husband OR trespasses against him, by virtue of the stone she is the sooner reconciled to have her husband's grace. Preserve the disjunction, same woman/husband, qualified sooner, causal attribution and purpose/result wording. No particular event, exact time, guaranteed immediate success or modern efficacy is asserted.
scope_alternatives_not_resolved: The though clause may concede the magnet's generic attracting disposition, or an operative tendency while the counter-influence is present. The paragraph does not decide a modern force model. Neither branch licenses deleting the magnet proposition or asserting a measured force balance.
Drawing away is the written direction. It does not itself prove prior attachment or require an explicitly narrated before/after trajectory.
So that introduces the restatement/explanation in this edition; it is not automatically a temporal next-step operator.

The human example may be taken as a literal attributed virtue or a culturally mediated claim. The content should retain what the author asserts without validating it or silently treating it as only metaphor.
design.consequence_beyond_repeated_names: Under the same conditional iron context, a full account must retain both the magnet-drawing concession and the adamant-attributed prevention/away relation with one iron referent. Treating each material as an independent label or assigning a single unqualified attraction outcome loses the ownership and opposition. The later human clause adds a different qualified outcome under the same stone kind; it does not permit a universal separation or universal reunion gloss.

rivals.reading: Each draw/it introduces a new iron patient.
rivals.difference: Avoids the shared-patient conflict by breaking the explicit local reference chain.

rivals.reading: Magnet attraction guarantees approach in every context.
rivals.difference: Cannot retain the stated prevention under adamant placement; the source does not give such an unconditional implication.

rivals.reading: The concession says the magnet has no attracting property.
rivals.difference: Negates instead of preserving the conceded magnet claim. Whether an actual simultaneous attempt is asserted remains open.

rivals.reading: Both influences draw the same iron toward the magnet.
rivals.difference: Loses the explicit away/from relation and the iron-to-itself reflexive owner.

rivals.reading: The stone always separates participants, or always reunites them.
rivals.difference: Collapses the directed mineral claim and qualified human reconciliation into one unsupported universal effect.

rivals.reading: Away AND trespass are jointly required, followed by immediate guaranteed reunion.
rivals.difference: Changes the written OR and sooner qualification.

rivals.reading: Independent complete clauses express all claims without any reusable written constructor.
rivals.difference: Still source-compatible. This RAW has no observed target writing evidence to choose composition over this rival.

predecessors_read.difference: Already owns attraction modes and material priority: one receiver with different candidates. This proposal instead fixes one patient and distinguishes two named influence owners and opposed directions under placement; no novelty for attraction or context dependence alone.

Concession is already owned. That source grants part of a nourishment explanation and infers residual transfer; this is a shared-patient competing-direction claim, without numerical residual or unseen channel inference.

Tin operation-specific effects and two prerequisite classes remain prior work. The present difference is simultaneous ownership of opposite directed relations to one written patient, with the disposition/operative scope explicitly unresolved.
Carrier/payload/site/soul distinction is different from two influence owners sharing one directional patient. No new claim for identity by itself.

design.structural_connection_and_debt: Known directed composition, whole-form residuals and context effects make role-sensitive or concessive constructions legitimate exploratory possibilities, but do not identify any semantic operator, segment or target referent. No target passage, glossary, shared writer, code family, image owner or segmentation is chosen here. A later whole reading would have to bind all paragraph duties, not merely repeated material names.
historical_and_semantic_limits: Adamant is retained as this edition names it, without equating it with a modern mineral species or asserting that the stated magnetic or marital effects are true.

The English pronouns, reflexive, conditional and concession are actually written reference devices in the owned edition; they are not evidence that Voynich uses English syntax or the same glyph forms.
The source is short but includes two domains. A writer that leaves the whole human claim free would not cover the complete unit.
No changed manuscript input or target binding is supplied. Exact novelty remains unreviewed; a complete-clause rival remains available.
